The evidence explicitly mentions 'hardware blending' and 'pixel read-back' to evaluate this recurrence. In computer graphics, accumulating values in a frame buffer via blending over many steps is a well-known source of floating-point precision errors. The evidence supports the mechanism (accumulation in frame buffer via blending) that leads to the claim (precision errors). Although the evidence doesn't explicitly use the word 'error', it describes the exact computational process (iterative accumulation in a fixed-precision buffer) where such errors are an inherent physical limitation of the hardware described. The claim is a direct consequence of the method described in the evidence.
